dip.name: Winners at a discount
dip.idea: A stock on a strong run takes a small step back. The strategy signals that dip.
dip.rationale: Pick winning stocks: companies whose price has climbed steadily for months because the market believes in them. Then wait for a short pullback, when the price dips a few percent.

rules.text: **It's a proven winner:** it rose at least `{minGainPct}%` from its low, and its averages are stacked and rising (`SMA {floorDays}` > `SMA 150` > `SMA {trendDays}`).
**Wait for a discount:** it drops into the discount zone, `{zoneStartPct}-{zoneEndPct}%` below its recent peak.
**The dip is not a collapse:** it is still above its `SMA {floorDays}` (average price over the last {floorDays} days).

backtest.universe: 1,146 US stocks (S&P 500, S&P 400, Nasdaq-100, and dropouts)
backtest.testedDefaults: The tested defaults: €3,000 budget, €100 steps, up to 5 per stock.

minGainPct.sentence: Proven growth: the recent peak is at least {value} above the low.
minGainPct.help: Higher: only the strongest runs count, so fewer candidates. Lower: more stocks qualify, with weaker trends.

gainDays.sentence: The low is the lowest close of the last {value}.
gainDays.help: 21 trading days is about a month (168 ≈ 8 months). Longer: an older low counts, so a slower climb can qualify. Shorter: the rise must be recent.

trendDays.sentence: The long average is the SMA over {value}.
trendDays.help: The bottom of the stack, and it must be rising. Longer: steadier, slower to turn, so a trend counts later and stays a candidate longer.

peakDays.sentence: The recent peak is the highest close of the last {value}.
peakDays.help: What the dip is measured from. Longer: an older, often higher peak, so the same price reads as a deeper dip.

zoneStartPct.sentence: The discount zone starts {value} below the recent peak.
zoneStartPct.help: The smallest dip that counts. Lower: signals sooner, on shallow dips. Higher: waits for a bigger discount, so fewer signals.

zoneEndPct.sentence: It ends {value} below the recent peak.
zoneEndPct.help: The deepest dip that counts. Higher: also buys deeper falls, as long as they stay above the floor average.

floorDays.sentence: The floor average is the SMA over {value}.
floorDays.help: The top of the candidate's stack and the zone's floor: a close below it is a collapse, not a dip. Shorter: the floor follows the price closely, so deep dips fall through it.

cooldownDays.sentence: After a step, wait {value} before the next buy signal.
cooldownDays.help: Counted from the step's buy. Shorter: steps come closer together. Longer: a stock's steps spread out over more dips.

candidate.title: 1 · Candidate: which stocks it watches
candidate.lead: A stock is a candidate, a proven winner, while all three hold: it rose at least the growth below from its low; its averages are stacked, the floor average above a middle one above the long average (`SMA 50` > `SMA 150` > `SMA 200` when tested; the middle one stays between the other two); and the long average is higher than 20 trading days ago. A stock that isn't a candidate gets no signal, however far it dips.

signal.title: 2 · Buy signal: when a candidate signals
signal.lead: A candidate signals a buy when its close is in the discount zone: between the zone's start and end below its recent peak, and still above the floor average. The signal ends when the price leaves the zone, back up toward the peak or down through the floor.

pace.title: 3 · Pace: how often it buys
pace.lead: Each signal buys one step. A stock gets at most one step per stay in the zone, and up to your budget's steps in all.

gain.label: Proven growth
gain.info: The recent peak must be at least {min}% above the lowest close of the last months: only proven winners count.

stacked.label: Averages stacked
stacked.detail: Short {level} · middle {midLevel} · long {endLevel} (needs short > middle > long).
stacked.none: Needs the short average above the middle one, and that above the long one.
stacked.info: The SMA 50, SMA 150 and SMA 200 (average closes over those days), in that order: a steady uptrend.

rising.label: Long average rising
rising.detail: {+value}% vs 20 trading days ago ({endLevel} → {level}, needs above 0%).
rising.none: Needs the long average higher than 20 trading days ago.
rising.info: The long average (SMA 200) must be higher than 20 trading days ago so the long-term trend is pointing up.

zone.label: In the discount zone
zone.detail: {value}% below the recent peak. The zone is {min}–{max}% below ({level} to {endLevel}).
zone.past: {value}% below the recent peak — fell past the {min}–{max}% discount zone ({level} to {endLevel}).
zone.info: The discount zone is a dip of {min}–{max}% below the highest close of the last weeks.

floor.label: Above the floor average
floor.detail: {+value}% vs the floor average ({level}, needs 0% or higher).
floor.info: A dip that falls through the SMA 50 is a collapse, not a discount.

cooldown.label: Wait after a step
cooldown.detail: {value} more days to wait after the last step ({min} in all).
cooldown.info: After each step the rules wait a few calendar days before the next buy signal.

comeback.name: The comeback
comeback.idea: A stock that fell a lot starts to recover. The strategy looks for a confirmed turnaround.
comeback.rationale: A stock that fell a long way starts to climb again. Instead of guessing the bottom, the strategy waits until the turnaround looks confirmed, then signals buys in steps.

rules.text: **It was beaten down:** the stock fell at least `{drawdownPct}%` from its high of the last year.
**It turned around:** it climbs `{aboveSma50Pct}%` above its `SMA 50` (average price over the last 50 days).
**More people are trading it:** its volume (shares traded per day) is rising.

backtest.universe: 1,146 US stocks (S&P 500, S&P 400, Nasdaq-100, and dropouts)
backtest.testedDefaults: The tested defaults: €3,000 budget, €100 steps, up to 5 per stock.

drawdownPct.sentence: Beaten down: at least {value} below its 52-week high.
drawdownPct.help: Higher: only deep falls count, so fewer candidates. Lower: milder dips count too.

candidateDays.sentence: It stays a candidate for {value} after it was last beaten down.
candidateDays.help: Longer: a slower recovery can still signal. 0: it must turn while still beaten down.

aboveSma50Pct.sentence: The buy line is {value} above the SMA 50.
aboveSma50Pct.help: Higher: waits for a stronger move, skipping more dead-cat bounces, but buys later and higher.

volumeRatio.sentence: The 5-day average volume is at least {value} the 50-day.
volumeRatio.help: More trading confirms the turn. Higher: fewer, better-backed signals. 1: volume only has to be normal.

maxChasePct.sentence: Chase limit: buy only up to {value} above the buy line or a milestone's level.
maxChasePct.help: Higher: still buys a turn that jumped well past its line. Lower: skips turns that move too fast.

nearHighPct.sentence: Milestone near the old high: within {value} of the 52-week high.
nearHighPct.help: Higher: this milestone comes earlier in the recovery.

breakoutPullbackPct.sentence: Milestone breakout: a pullback of at least {value}, then a close above the high before it.
breakoutPullbackPct.help: Higher: needs a deeper pullback first, so the breakout comes less often.

cooldownDays.sentence: After a step, wait {value} before the next buy signal.
cooldownDays.help: Counted from the step's buy. Longer: steps spread out, even when milestones come close together.

candidate.title: 1 · Candidate: which stocks it watches
candidate.lead: A stock is a candidate, beaten down, when its close is at least the drop below its 52-week high and below its `SMA 200`. It stays a candidate for a while after that, so it can still signal once it recovers. A stock that isn't a candidate gets no signal.

signal.title: 2 · Buy signal: the first step
signal.lead: A candidate signals its first step when it turns: the close is at least the turn above its `SMA 50` (the buy line), on rising volume, and not too far above the line. The signal ends when the price or the volume falls back, or the price runs past the chase limit.

milestones.title: 3 · Milestones: the next steps
milestones.lead: Once bought, each new sign that the turn is real earns one more step: back above the `SMA 200`, a golden cross (`SMA 50` above `SMA 200`), near the old high, or a breakout after a pullback. Each is bought only up to the chase limit above its level.

pace.title: 4 · Pace: how often it buys
pace.lead: A step is one buy, up to your budget's steps per stock.

beaten.label: Beaten down lately
beaten.detail: Candidate since {date} ({value} of {max} trading days). Now {+subValue}% from the 52-week high ({level}) and {+endValue}% vs the SMA 200 ({endLevel}).
beaten.past: Window closed: last beaten down on {date} ({value} trading days ago; window is {max} days).
beaten.none: Not beaten down in its price history. Needs both conditions below on the same day to start a {max}-day window.
beaten.info: Beaten down: at least {min}% below its 52-week high and below its SMA 200 on the same day. Once triggered, it stays a candidate for {max} trading days while it recovers.

drop.label: Drop from the 52-week high
drop.detail: {+value}% from the 52-week high ({level}, needs −{min}% or lower).
drop.info: To become beaten down, the close must fall at least {min}% below the highest close of the last 52 weeks.

vsSma200.label: Price vs SMA 200
vsSma200.detail: {+value}% vs the SMA 200 ({level}, needs below 0% when beaten down).
vsSma200.info: The average close of the last 200 days, the long trend. A stock must fall below it (while at least {min}% off its 52-week high) to count as beaten down.

buyLine.label: Price vs the buy line
buyLine.detail: {+value}% vs the buy line ({level}). A step needs 0% to +{max}% ({level} to {endLevel}).
buyLine.past: {+value}% above the buy line ({level}) — past the +{max}% chase limit ({endLevel}).
buyLine.pastShort: too far past the buy line ({+value}%)
buyLine.info: The buy line is {min}% above the SMA 50 ({midLevel}), the average close of the last 50 days: the stock has turned. Above +{max}% past the buy line is too late to chase.

chase.label: Not too far past the line
chase.detail: {+value}% above the buy line: more than {max}% is too late to chase.
chase.short: too far past the buy line

volume.label: Volume: 5-day vs 50-day average
volume.info: Shares traded per day: more trading than usual backs the turn.

sma200.label: Back above the SMA 200
sma200.detail: {+value}% vs the SMA 200 ({level}). Step window: 0% to +{max}% ({level} to {endLevel}).
sma200.past: {+value}% above the SMA 200 ({level}) — past the +{max}% chase limit ({endLevel}).
sma200.info: Milestone: reclaiming the 200-day average confirms the long-term recovery and earns one step if bought within +{max}%.

golden.label: Golden cross
golden.detail: SMA 50 ({level}) is {+subValue}% vs SMA 200 ({midLevel}). Price {+value}% vs SMA 50 (window 0% to +{max}%, up to {endLevel}).
golden.past: SMA 50 ({level}) is {+subValue}% vs SMA 200 ({midLevel}), but price is {+value}% above SMA 50 (past +{max}% limit, {endLevel}).
golden.info: Milestone: the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day average, confirming a medium-term uptrend.

near_high.label: Near the old high
near_high.detail: {+value}% vs the near-high line ({level}, within {min}% of {midLevel}). Step window: 0% to +{max}% (up to {endLevel}).
near_high.past: {+value}% above the near-high line ({level}) — past the +{max}% chase limit ({endLevel}).
near_high.info: Milestone: price recovers to within {min}% of the 52-week high.

breakout.label: Breakout
breakout.detail: {+value}% vs the high before its {min}% pullback ({level}). Step window: 0% to +{max}% ({level} to {endLevel}).
breakout.past: {+value}% above the high before its {min}% pullback ({level}) — past the +{max}% chase limit ({endLevel}).
breakout.none: Needs an {min}% pullback after the last buy, then a close above the high before it.
breakout.info: Milestone: after pulling back at least {min}% from a post-buy high, breaking above that high earns one step.

cooldown.label: Wait after a step
cooldown.detail: {value} more days to wait after the last step ({min} in all).
cooldown.info: After each step the rules wait a few calendar days before the next buy signal.

bear.name: Bear markets
bear.tagline: When the market is on sale
bear.idea: When the whole market falls 20%, the strategy signals buys of a broad S&P 500 fund in small steps as it recovers.
bear.rationale: Big market crashes are rare and scary, and most people sell. Instead of guessing the bottom, the strategy waits for the first bounce and then signals buys in small steps while prices are still low.

rules.text: **The market fell hard:** the S&P 500 is `{drawdownPct}%` or more below its high.
**The first bounce:** it climbs `{reboundPct}%` off its low. That's the first step.
**Then in steps:** one more step every `{stepEveryDays}` trading days, until the budget is used.

backtest.universe: Major equity indexes and 30 sector ETFs across 134 bear markets
backtest.testedDefaults: The tested defaults: €3,000 budget, 5 steps of €600.

stockStatus.watching: In a drop: {n}% above its low

drawdownPct.sentence: A drop is at least {value} below the recent high.
drawdownPct.help: Higher: only real crashes count, so signals come rarely (years apart). Lower: smaller corrections count too.

highDays.sentence: The recent high is the highest close of the last {value}.
highDays.help: 21 trading days is about a month (126 ≈ 6 months). Longer: the fall is measured from an older, often higher peak.

reboundPct.sentence: The first step comes {value} above the drop's lowest close.
reboundPct.help: Lower: buys sooner, nearer the bottom, but may catch a fall that isn't over. Higher: waits for a clearer recovery.

stepEveryDays.help: 10 trading days is about 2 weeks. Shorter: the budget goes in faster. Longer: spreads the buys over more of the recovery.

candidate.title: 1 · The drop: when it starts watching
candidate.lead: The fund is in a drop when its close is at least the drop below its recent high. From then on it tracks the lowest close. Without a drop, nothing signals.

signal.title: 2 · Buy signal: the first step
signal.lead: The first step comes when the close bounces the rebound above the drop's lowest close.

pace.title: 3 · Pace: the next steps
pace.lead: After the first step, one more step comes at a fixed pace until your budget's steps are bought. Then the cycle ends when the price gets back to its old high, or, once the drop is older than the recent-high period, when a new drop starts.

drop.label: In a drop
drop.detail: {value}% below its recent high ({level}). A drop is {min}% or more.
drop.info: The fall from the highest close of the last 6 months.

bounce.label: Bounce off the low
bounce.detail: {value}% above the drop's low ({endLevel}). The first step comes at +{min}% ({level}).
bounce.none: Once in a drop, the first step signals when the close climbs +{min}% off the drop's lowest close.
bounce.info: Instead of guessing the bottom of a crash, the first buy waits for a +{min}% rebound off the lowest close.

pace.label: Next step
pace.detail: {value} of {min} trading days since the last step.
pace.none: After the first bounce, signals one more step every {min} trading days until all steps are bought.
pace.short: {value} of {min} days to the next step
pace.info: Spreads the remaining steps across the recovery at a steady pace of one step every {min} trading days.

trend.name: Index trend
trend.tagline: Take the wins, dodge the losses
trend.idea: The strategy signals a buy of a broad index fund when the market moves into an uptrend, and a sale when the trend turns down.
trend.rationale: Markets move in long waves. The strategy signals a buy of a broad index fund when the market moves into an uptrend, and a sale when the trend turns down, to dodge the dip. After the dip it looks for a new buy signal.

smaDays.sentence: The trend line is the SMA over {value}.
smaDays.help: Longer: steadier, fewer signals, but later into and out of a trend. Shorter: reacts sooner, with more false turns.

bandPct.sentence: The buy and sell lines are {value} above and below the trend line.
bandPct.help: Wider: fewer trades and fewer false signals, but buys later and sells later. 0: trades every crossing.

cooldownDays.sentence: After a sale, wait {value} before the next buy signal.
cooldownDays.help: Counted from the sale. A sell signal is never delayed. Longer: fewer sell-then-buy-back trades when the market is choppy.

rules.text: The market closes more than `{bandPct}%` above its `SMA {smaDays}` (average price over the last {smaDays} days).
The market closes more than `{bandPct}%` below its `SMA {smaDays}`.
All in, all out: each signal covers the whole budget at once.

backtest.universe: 6 major global indexes (S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, EFA, DAX, Nikkei)
backtest.testedDefaults: The whole €3,000 budget, all in, all out.

signal.title: 1 · Buy and sell signals
signal.lead: The trend line is an average of the close. A buy signal comes when the close is more than the band above it, a sell signal when it's more than the band below. In between, nothing changes: the band stops a market that hovers around the line from flipping in and out.

pace.title: 2 · Pace: how often it trades
pace.lead: All in, all out: each signal covers the whole budget.

buyLine.label: Price vs the buy line
buyLine.detail: {+value}% vs the buy line ({level}, +{min}% above the SMA {midLevel}). Close is {+subValue}% vs the SMA.
buyLine.info: The trend line is the average close of the last 200 days. Signals a buy above +{min}%; inside the ±{min}% band ({endLevel} to {level}), the trend stays unchanged.

sellLine.label: Price vs the sell line
sellLine.detail: {+value}% vs the sell line ({level}, −{min}% below the SMA {midLevel}). Close is {+subValue}% vs the SMA.
sellLine.info: Signals a sale below −{min}% of the 200-day average; inside the ±{min}% band ({level} to {endLevel}), the position stays held.

ai.name: Your AI's top picks
ai.tagline: Let your AI do the reading
ai.idea: Every 2 weeks the AI scores each stock from 0 to 100, and the top score should get a position. Use your own AI.
ai.rationale: Nobody can read every news story and financial report about every company, but an AI can. You run our prompt in the AI you already use; it scores each stock, and the strategy signals the top one. You see whether all that reading turns into better picks.

topN.sentence: Each round, one step goes to each of the top {value} by overall score.

rules.text: Every `{everyDays} days` you run the AI round: copy the prompt, paste it into your AI, paste its answer back.
Each round, one step goes to each of the top `{topN}` by overall score, until the budget is used. A stock with all its steps passes its turn to the next.
If you skip a round, there's no signal that round.
